summary: Charles Dederich founded Synanon in 1958 as a California drug rehab program, then turned it into a violent cult that seized children, forced vasectomies, intimidated the press and tried to kill a lawyer with a rattlesnake.

evidence.note: Dederich's birth in Toledo, Ohio and childhood begin the biography
facility incorporated as a nonprofit in 1958; start of main span
the Game: confrontational group attack sessions described at length
Game and later the Trip sold to non-addicts as human-potential psychotherapy
children taken from parents into a communal hatchery and school
Punk Squad boot camp beats court-sent teenagers
lawsuits against the Examiner, later threats to Time and ABC staff
tax-exempt businesses run on unpaid member labor; later IRS back-tax bill
rattlesnake left in Morantz's mailbox, followed by arrests
no-contest plea to conspiracy to murder in 1980; end of main span
Dederich's death in 1997 closes the covered span
legacy in the troubled teen industry traced to recent years

notes: Synanon and Dederich treated as co-primary; lifetime rule gives 1913-1997. Opening history of addiction treatment (Rush, Freud, AA) is background, not counted. Transcript garbles years (rattlesnake attack and Betty's death read as 'ninety seven'); used 1977/1978 from context. Troubled teen legacy set reaches_present.
